v1r_login.title: Set up v1r: sign in to Tesla
v1r_login.description:
Home Assistant will create an RSA key and register it with your Powerwall through your Tesla account. After that, it talks to the gateway over your LAN.

Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.

1. Open [Tesla's sign-in page]({login_url}).
2. On that tab, press **F12** and choose the **Console** tab in the panel that opens.
3. Sign in to your Tesla account. When you finish, the page won't change. That's expected.
4. The Console shows a red line starting `Failed to launch 'tesla://auth/callback?code=`. Copy that whole line and paste it below.

After you submit, you'll have **about 10 minutes** to toggle the Powerwall's On/Off switch, so be ready to go to it.

data_description.callback_url: The whole `Failed to launch 'tesla://auth/callback?code=...'` line, or just the tesla:// address in it

v1r_site.title: Choose your Powerwall
v1r_site.description: Your Tesla account has more than one energy site. Choose the one to register the key with.

v1r_verify.title: Confirm at the Powerwall
v1r_verify.description:
The key has been sent to your Powerwall. To approve it, within **10 minutes**:

- **Powerwall 2:** turn the On/Off switch on the side of the battery **off for about 15 seconds**, then back on.
- **Powerwall 3:** turn the small black On/Off rocker under the red flap on the left side **off for about 15 seconds**, then back on. Not the large red knob.

A quick flick of a second or two is ignored. Don't leave it off long enough for the gateway to shut down.

Then select **Submit**. Home Assistant checks for about 2 minutes.

v1r_gateway.title: Connect to the gateway
v1r_gateway.description: The key is approved and saved at `{key_path}`. Now enter how to reach the gateway on your LAN.

data_description.host: The gateway's LAN IP address (the wired or Wi-Fi address on your network, not 192.168.91.1). Reserve it in your router so it doesn't change.
data_description.gw_pwd: Full gateway Wi-Fi password printed on the QR label. At least one of this and the customer password is required
data_description.password: Customer password. If omitted, the last 5 characters of the gateway password are used
data_description.wifi_host: Alternate WiFi TEDAPI host to fall back to

cloud_login.title: Sign in to Tesla
cloud_login.description:
Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.

1. Open [Tesla's sign-in page]({login_url}).
2. On that tab, press **F12** and choose the **Console** tab in the panel that opens.
3. Sign in to your Tesla account. When you finish, the page won't change. That's expected.
4. The Console shows a red line starting `Failed to launch 'tesla://auth/callback?code=`. Copy that whole line and paste it below.

Paste it within a few minutes. The link works once, so if anything goes wrong a fresh one is shown.

data_description.callback_url: The whole `Failed to launch 'tesla://auth/callback?code=...'` line, or just the tesla:// address in it

cloud.description: Uses Tesla's cloud API with a `.pypowerwall.auth` file you already have, for example one created by `python -m pypowerwall setup`. To sign in from Home Assistant instead, go back and choose "Cloud mode (sign in with Tesla account)".

data_description.authpath: Directory containing the .pypowerwall.auth file created by `python -m pypowerwall setup`
data_description.siteid: Tesla site ID to use if the account has more than one site

fleetapi.description: Uses Tesla's FleetAPI instead of a local connection. Requires a one-time setup performed outside Home Assistant first: register an app at developer.tesla.com, then run `python -m pypowerwall.fleetapi setup` to create a `.pypowerwall.fleetapi` file, and point this at the directory containing it.

data_description.authpath: Directory containing the .pypowerwall.fleetapi file created by `python -m pypowerwall.fleetapi setup`
data_description.siteid: Tesla site ID to use if the account has more than one site

tedapi_v1r.description: Full-protobuf LAN access for Powerwall 3 and Powerwall 2, using a pre-registered RSA key. Requires a one-time setup performed outside Home Assistant first: run `python -m pypowerwall register` to generate and register an RSA-4096 key pair with the gateway (this may require briefly power-cycling the gateway to confirm), then point this at the resulting private key file. To create and register the key from Home Assistant instead, go back and choose "TEDAPI v1r LAN (set up with Tesla account)".

data_description.host: Hostname or IP address of the Powerwall gateway
data_description.gw_pwd: Full gateway Wi-Fi password printed on the QR label. At least one of this and the customer password is required
data_description.password: Customer password. If omitted, the last 5 characters of the gateway password are used
data_description.rsa_key_path: Path to the RSA-4096 private key PEM file produced by `python -m pypowerwall register`
data_description.wifi_host: Alternate WiFi TEDAPI host to fall back to

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure connection
reconfigure.description:
Update the connection settings for this Powerwall ({conn_type} mode). Useful if the gateway password changed, the gateway moved to a new IP address, or a Cloud/FleetAPI config cache directory moved.

This must still reach the same physical gateway -- to switch to a different connection mode or a different Powerwall, remove this entry and add it again.

reconfigure_tesla_login.title: Sign in to Tesla for export windows
reconfigure_tesla_login.description:
The export window actions change your Tesla tariff, which goes through Tesla's cloud rather than the gateway. This saves a Tesla sign-in for them, replacing any earlier one. The LAN connection to the gateway is unchanged.

Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.

1. Open [Tesla's sign-in page]({login_url}).
2. On that tab, press **F12** and choose the **Console** tab in the panel that opens.
3. Sign in to your Tesla account. When you finish, the page won't change. That's expected.
4. The Console shows a red line starting `Failed to launch 'tesla://auth/callback?code=`. Copy that whole line and paste it below.

Paste it within a few minutes. The link works once, so if anything goes wrong a fresh one is shown. Home Assistant then checks the sign-in every 6 hours, which keeps it working, and raises a repair if Tesla stops accepting it.

data_description.callback_url: The whole `Failed to launch 'tesla://auth/callback?code=...'` line, or just the tesla:// address in it

error.auth_cache_not_found: No .pypowerwall.auth (Cloud) or .pypowerwall.fleetapi (FleetAPI) file found in that directory. Enter the path as Home Assistant sees it, for example /config/pypowerwall.
error.auth_cache_not_writable: Home Assistant can't write to that directory. It needs write access to save refreshed Tesla tokens.
error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect. Check the connection details and try again.
error.invalid_callback: No sign-in code found. Paste the whole Console line that contains tesla://auth/callback?code=...
error.login_failed: Tesla didn't accept the sign-in. Use the new link and try again. The Home Assistant log has the details.
error.state_mismatch: That address came from an older sign-in link. Use the new link and paste the address it leads to.
error.missing_password: Enter the gateway password, the customer password, or both.
error.rsa_key_not_found: No file found at that path. Enter the path to the RSA private key as Home Assistant sees it, for example /config/tedapi_rsa_private.pem.
error.no_energy_site: No Powerwall was found on that Tesla account.
error.v1r_register_failed: Tesla didn't accept the key registration. Select Submit to try again. The Home Assistant log has the details.
error.v1r_window_closed: The 10 minute window closed before the Powerwall confirmed, so the key has been sent again. Toggle the switch now, then select Submit.
error.v1r_not_verified: The Powerwall hasn't confirmed the key yet. Toggle the switch off for about 15 seconds and back on, then select Submit to check again.

progress.wait_for_verified: Waiting for the Powerwall to confirm the key. This takes up to 2 minutes.

abort.already_configured: This Powerwall gateway is already configured
abort.v1r_already_configured: This Powerwall is already set up in Home Assistant (for example as a Cloud entry). Delete that entry first, then run this setup again. The new entry keeps the same entity IDs.
abort.tesla_sign_in_saved: Tesla sign-in saved. The export window actions will use it.
abort.wrong_gateway: Those settings connect to a different Powerwall gateway than this entry was set up for. Reconfigure only updates how to reach the same gateway -- to add a different one, add a new entry instead.

data_description.design_capacity_kwh: Original rated capacity of one battery, used as the 100% reference for the Battery health sensor. Powerwall 2 and 3 are 13.5 kWh.

schedule_max_backup.name: Schedule max backup
schedule_max_backup.description: Starts a manual backup event (storm watch / max backup mode), maximizing the battery reserve for a fixed duration. Requires TEDAPI v1r LAN mode.

duration_seconds.name: Duration
duration_seconds.description: How long the max backup event should run, in seconds. Defaults to 7200 (2 hours).

cancel_max_backup.name: Cancel max backup
cancel_max_backup.description: Cancels the current manual backup event (storm watch / max backup mode) started by schedule_max_backup. Requires TEDAPI v1r LAN mode.

set_export_window.name: Set export window
set_export_window.description: Temporarily changes the Tesla tariff so the Powerwall treats a time window as the most valuable time to export, for example an Octopus Power Down event. The original tariff is saved and put back when the window ends. Needs Time-Based Control with export set to Everything, and a Tesla sign-in (Cloud mode, or the sign-in saved by the v1r setup).

start.name: Start
start.description: When the window starts. Defaults to now. The tariff changes straight away; the Powerwall reacts to the window when it arrives.

end.name: End
end.description: When the window ends. The original tariff is restored at this time. Must be less than 24 hours after the start.

price.name: Price
price.description: Buy and sell price per kWh during the window, in the tariff's currency. Set it well above your normal rates. Defaults to 2.0.

restore_tariff.name: Restore tariff
restore_tariff.description: Puts back the Tesla tariff saved by Set export window straight away, ending the export window early. Does nothing if no window is in place.

tesla_sign_in_failed.title: Tesla sign-in for export windows has stopped working
tesla_sign_in_failed.description:
Tesla no longer accepts the sign-in that {title} uses to change your tariff, so the export window actions can't start a window or restore your tariff afterwards.

Go to Settings → Devices & services → Tesla Powerwall, open {title}'s ⋮ menu, choose **Reconfigure**, then **Sign in to Tesla (for export windows)**. This notice clears at the next successful check, within 6 hours, or when an export window action next connects.

If an export window was in place, check your tariff in the Tesla app and re-select your energy plan there if needed.
